headlines.title: Arista Networks And 2 Other AI Infrastructure Stocks To Own
headlines.summary: Data centre companies recently fell after US election results raised expectations of tighter oversight. That kind of policy scare can shift attention to the quieter workhorses of artificial intelligence: the switches, optical links and server hardware that keep AI models running. For investors, this corner of the market offers direct exposure to AI infrastructure demand. This article walks through three hardware stocks filtered from our AI networking and server-focused screener.

headlines.title: Arista Networks (ANET) Stock Price Rallies After Q3 Earnings Shock
headlines.summary: Arista Networks stock jumped 5% to US$178.48 after investors digested its Q3 2026 report. Traders reacted to a blowout headline, with revenue of US$3.66b and operating margin around 49% grabbing attention across the cloud networking space. Yet the real story sits beyond today’s bounce.

headlines.title: Arista Networks Blows Out Earnings and Rises While Most AI Suppliers Fall After Midterms
headlines.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., looks at why Arista Networks (NYSE: ANET) earnings could make the stock a safe haven in the AI trade. Arista makes the high-speed switches that connect AI servers inside data centers, and its quarter beat across the board.

description: Arista Networks, Inc. engages in the development, marketing, and sale of data-driven, client to cloud networking solutions for AI, data center, campus, and routing environments in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia-Pacific. Its cloud networking solutions consist of Extensible Operating System (EOS), a publish-subscribe state-sharing networking operating system offered in combination with a set of network applications. The company offers data center, cloud and AI networking, cognitive adjacencies, and cognitive network software and services. It also provides post contract customer support services, such as technical support, hardware repair and replacement parts beyond standard warranty, bug fixes, patches, and upgrade services. The company serves a range of industries comprising internet companies, cloud service providers, financial services organizations, government agencies, media and entertainment, healthcare, oil and gas, education, manufacturing, industrial, and others. It markets and sells its products through distributors, system integrators, value-added resellers, and original equipment manufacturer partners, as well as through its direct sales force. Arista Networks, Inc. was formerly known as Arastra, Inc. and changed its name to Arista Networks, Inc. in October 2008. The company was incorporated in 2004 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.
